paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The old tabernacle, with its rooms, its curtain and its once-a-year trip for the high priest, was an "illustration for the present time" (Hebrews 9:9). It was pointing at something, not finishing the job. The gifts and sacrifices there "were unable to cleanse the conscience of the worshiper" (Hebrews 9:9).

Then comes the turn. Christ entered the Most Holy Place "once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption" (Hebrews 9:12). ONE time, friend. I've scrubbed one oven a hundred times and it still has crumbs, and He did this once and it STAYED done. And He didn't just bring an offering, He offered Himself unblemished to God (Hebrews 9:14).

So what does that mean for you? His blood can "purify our consciences from works of death, so that we may serve the living God" (Hebrews 9:14). That means you don't have to keep scrubbing at guilt that He already dealt with. You get to serve God with a clean conscience, and that is something worth being loud about.
